issues.description: The fixed-point integer typedefs are declared with an invalid/atypical token order (e.g. 'typedef int long long fix_t;') in multiple provided source files. This is a structural type declaration problem that can prevent the code from compiling and will confuse students because the problem statement explicitly requires the assignment to compile. The incorrect typedef appears both in the example/test headers and in the implementation, so students following the template may be blocked by a compilation error rather than an intended exercise gap.
issues.suggestedFix: Use standard, unambiguous typedef declarations for fixed-point integer types in all repositories. For example replace 'typedef int long long fix_t;' with 'typedef long long fix_t;' and replace 'typedef unsigned int long long fixu_t;' with 'typedef unsigned long long fixu_t;'. Apply the correction consistently in example_program/src/math_fix.c, tests/src/math_fix.h and any other occurrences so the project compiles as required.

issues.description: The Bitmap24::set parameter names (and their implied meanings) are inconsistent between the header declaration and the implementation/usage. In Bitmap24.hpp the method is declared as set(int i_x, int i_y, ...), while the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp defines set(int i_y, int i_x, ...). The call site in main.cpp uses bitmap.set(i, j, ...), where i is the row (y) and j is the column (x) — matching the implementation but contradicting the header parameter names. This mismatch creates confusion for students reading the API vs. the implementation and for anyone relying on the header's parameter names as documentation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter names (and their order/meaning) consistent across header, implementation and usage. For example, change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to match the implementation: void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); or (preferably) use clearer names for both declaration and definition such as void set(int row, int col, char r, char g, char b); and update any call sites accordingly. Ensure both template and solution repositories use the same corrected signature and parameter names.
